This run's planted-defect fixture design (a disclosed conflict between a policy document and a pre-existing regression fixture, both named explicitly in scope.json's acceptance criteria) was resolved correctly by the real Engineer before any code was written, because the Engineer proactively read the full findings.json (including an Architect-authored inferred finding naming the exact conflict) and the referenced regression fixture file -- demonstrating the cardinal 'verify before building' principle working as intended, but defeating this specific fixture's ability to produce a genuine routable logic_bug with this real agent's actual behavior.
follow_up_actions: Attempt a new run (new run_id) reusing the same isolated fixture area, with a redesigned task that transparently and explicitly directs the Engineer to implement the policy document's literal (disclosed, known-incorrect) boundary rather than relying on the Engineer independently discovering and resolving a hidden conflict -- since this run's evidence shows a real, capable Engineer reliably discovers and resolves such conflicts on its own.
